draft.title: Pork Green Mango Soup

ingredients.note: Unripe/sour green mangoes, cut into 1-inch strips
Optional garnish for color and heat

steps.text: Cook rice according to standard pot or rice cooker instructions.
Chop the bone-in pork ribs into small bite-sized pieces.

why.text: The bones add more flavor to the broth.
why.quote: you want the porks with the bone on them 'cause the bone gives a little bit more flavor to the broth

steps.text: Bring a pot of salted water to a quick boil with the pork pieces, skim off foam and scum, pour away the water, and repeat parboiling with fresh water.

why.text: Removes blood, scum, and extra proteins to keep broth clear and avoid weird off-flavors.
why.quote: makes it a little cloudy I don't like those extra proteins and collagens and all that stuff floating around I like crystal clear broth

steps.text: Heat oil in a pot or pan over medium-high heat (insert wooden chopstick to check if oil bubbles around it). Sear parboiled pork ribs until golden brown on all sides.
Add cracked black pepper, then pour in fish sauce. Sauté for about 30 seconds until fish sauce reduces slightly and pepper becomes fragrant.
Add sliced white onions to the pan and cook until slightly translucent, scraping up brown fond on the bottom.
Add water, return pork pieces to pot, and bring to a gentle simmer until meat is tender.

dials.effect: Pork becomes soft and easy to chew

steps.text: Add 1-inch green mango strips to the soup and simmer until softened.

why.text: Raw green mangoes are hard and crunchy; cooking releases their sour flavor into the soup.
why.quote: 'cause that's what the signature of the soup is

dials.effect: Softens green mango texture from crunchy to tender

steps.text: Turn off heat and stir in freshly cut white onion strips, cilantro, and green onions.

why.text: White onions are less sweet, complementing the sour fruit.
why.quote: 'cause I don't like onions to be a little too sweet in this soup 'cause there's a fruit component and the fruits are a sweet and sour

steps.text: Ladle soup over cooked rice and top with sliced chili peppers for garnish if desired.

notes: Corrected dictation error 'fish house tries' to 'fish sauce dries' and 'reese's' to 'releases'.
Corrected order: grouped ingredient prep (chopping cilantro, green onions, mangoes) into cooking flow.

questions.quote: cut up pork ribs into tiny little chunks... add water to the soup
questions.question: How much pork ribs and how much water/broth should be used for this soup?
questions.why_it_matters: Using too much water will dilute the soup broth, while too little will cause the broth to boil off before the pork becomes tender.
questions.suggestion: 2 pounds bone-in pork ribs and 6 to 8 cups of water.

questions.quote: throw in the onions and then you sear the onions around... and then once that onion becomes slightly translucent... then you throw in your freshly cut white onions
questions.question: Are white onions added at two different times (some sautéed early with the pork, and some raw at the end), or should all onions be added at the end?
questions.why_it_matters: Sautéing onions makes them sweet, which the cook specifically mentioned wanting to avoid to balance the sour green mangoes.
questions.suggestion: Use half an onion sautéed early for flavor foundation, and reserve half thinly sliced to add fresh at the end.

questions.quote: cut mangoes into one inch strips green mangoes you want the mangoes to be really sour
questions.question: How many green mangoes should be added, and is there a specific variety or firm stage to look for?
questions.why_it_matters: The green mango provides the signature sour flavor; using ripe mangoes or the wrong quantity will make the soup overly sweet instead of pleasantly tart.
questions.suggestion: 2 large raw, hard green mangoes (such as green Kent or Tommy Atkins, or Asian sour green mangoes).

questions.quote: give it about like a 32nd so that the fish house tries and the cracked black pepper uh reese's it's aroma
questions.question: Did the cook mean '30 seconds so that the fish sauce dries and black pepper releases its aroma'?
questions.why_it_matters: Misinterpreting timing or ingredient steps could burn the seasonings or leave fish sauce raw and overpowering.
questions.suggestion: Cook fish sauce and black pepper for 30 seconds.

questions.quote: put your fish sauce in... first you add your pepper then your fish sauce
questions.question: How much fish sauce and black pepper should be added?
questions.why_it_matters: Fish sauce provides all the primary saltiness for the soup base; adding too little leaves it bland, and too much makes it overly salty.
questions.suggestion: 2 tablespoons fish sauce and 1/2 teaspoon coarsely cracked black pepper.

draft.title: Tomato Tofu

ingredients.note: Cook prepared some lightly yellow/spongy and some crispy golden
Added in batches as they reduced
Increased from 2 to 5 because garlic was old
Cook gestured amount ('just about that much')
Added to prevent drying and help coat tofu

steps.text: Slice the tofu into pieces. Dice about 5 tomatoes, slice the onions into thin strips, and peel 5 garlic cloves.
Heat frying oil in a deep pan until hot enough that a wooden chopstick produces bubbles. Deep fry the tofu pieces according to preference. Remove and set aside.

dials.effect: Spongy and creamier on the inside

steps.text: In a separate pan, heat a small amount of oil until hot enough for a chopstick to sizzle. Add the fish sauce right before the pan gets too hot and let it bubble briefly until it starts sticking to the bottom.
Immediately add the sliced onions with their juices into the pan to prevent the fish sauce from burning, then add 5 garlic cloves. Stir-fry for 5 to 7 minutes until soft and golden.

why.text: The onion juices cool down the pan so the fish sauce does not burn.
why.quote: you want to get all the juices to cool down the pan so it doesn't burn the fish sauce

steps.text: Add the diced tomatoes to the pan. Cook for about 2 minutes to allow them to slightly caramelize before adding a splash of water if the pan gets too dry.

why.text: Caramelizing the tomatoes gives the sauce a rich meaty depth.
why.quote: caramelize tomato adds a really meaty touch to the dish

steps.text: Add the fried tofu into the pan with the tomato sauce and add a small amount of water. Simmer for 5 to 10 minutes until the sauce coats and penetrates the tofu.

why.text: Simmering extracts flavor from the tomato fish sauce deep into the tofu pieces.
why.quote: so the water extract all the flavor from the sauce tomato fish sauce into the inner parts of the tofu

steps.text: Serve hot over steamed white rice, with soy sauce and sliced chili in a small dipping dish if desired.

notes: Reordered steps: Moved tofu deep-frying before sauce assembly so fried tofu is ready to simmer in sauce.
Self-correction: Garlic count increased from 2 to 5 because garlic was old.
Self-correction: Sauteing time adjusted from 5 minutes to 7 minutes for extra sweetness.
Self-correction: Tomato quantity increased to 5 total after initial batch reduced down.

questions.quote: chop the in onions into little strips
questions.question: What type of onion should be used (e.g. yellow onion, sweet onion, or green onions)?
questions.why_it_matters: Using green onions versus yellow onions changes when they are added and the sauce texture.
questions.suggestion: 1 medium yellow onion, sliced into strips.

questions.question: How much fish sauce should be added?
questions.why_it_matters: Too much fish sauce makes the dish overly salty and pungent, while too little lacks savory depth.

questions.question: What block size and firmness of tofu should be used?
questions.why_it_matters: Soft tofu will crumble when deep fried, whereas firm or extra-firm tofu holds its shape and crisps properly.

questions.question: Should the tofu be dried with paper towels before deep frying?
questions.why_it_matters: Wet tofu placed in hot deep-frying oil will splatter hot oil dangerously.
questions.suggestion: Pat the sliced tofu dry with paper towels before placing it into hot oil.

draft.title: Homemade Incubated Yogurt

ingredients.note: Can reduce amount if you prefer less sweet yogurt.

steps.text: Heat the milk in a pot until it steams slightly, making sure it does not boil.

why.quote: make sure it doesn't boil uh just until it steams a little bit

steps.text: Add 1/3 cup of sugar and mix in the plain yogurt, stirring until fully blended.
Pour the mixture into small jars.
Place all the small jars into the incubator and let sit for 8 to 12 hours.
Store the jars in the refrigerator or freezer before serving.

notes: Retained dictation phrase '10 in yogurt container' as a small container pending clarification.
Kept original order of steps while flagging missing cooling step before adding yogurt starter.

questions.question: Do you let the milk cool down before stirring in the starter yogurt?
questions.why_it_matters: Stirring yogurt cultures into steaming hot milk will kill the live bacteria, preventing the yogurt from setting.
questions.suggestion: Cool the milk to about 110°F (warm to the touch) before adding the yogurt starter.

questions.quote: small 10 in yogurt container that is not flavored at all
questions.question: What brand or exact size of plain yogurt do you use as the starter (e.g., 6 oz or 10 oz)?
questions.why_it_matters: The ratio of starter culture to milk determines how fast and well the yogurt ferments.
questions.suggestion: One 5.3 oz or 6 oz single-serve container of plain Greek yogurt with active live cultures.

questions.question: What type of milk do you use for this recipe?
questions.why_it_matters: Whole milk produces a thick, rich yogurt, whereas 2% or skim milk makes a thinner yogurt unless milk powder or extra processing is added.

questions.question: What kind of incubator or appliance are you using, and does it have a specific temperature setting?
questions.why_it_matters: Yogurt starter bacteria require a steady temperature between 105°F and 112°F to culture correctly.
questions.suggestion: An electric yogurt maker or Instant Pot set to the 'Yogurt' setting (around 110°F).

final.title: Homemade Incubated Yogurt

ingredients.note: Single small container used as starter.
Can reduce amount if you prefer less sweet yogurt.

steps.text: Heat the milk in a pot until it steams slightly, making sure it does not boil.

why.quote: make sure it doesn't boil uh just until it steams a little bit

steps.text: Allow the milk to cool down before adding the yogurt starter.

why.text: Adding active yogurt starter to hot milk kills the live bacterial cultures needed for fermentation.

steps.text: Add 1/3 cup of sugar and mix in the plain yogurt, stirring until fully blended.
Pour the mixture into small jars.
Place all the small jars into an incubator and let sit for 8 to 12 hours.
steps.suggested_detail: electric yogurt maker or Instant Pot set to the 'Yogurt' setting (around 110°F)

steps.text: Store the jars in the refrigerator or freezer before serving.

notes: Corrected speech-to-text error '10 in' to single cup plain Dannon yogurt per user response.
Inserted missing cooling step prior to adding starter yogurt based on user confirmation.
Specified milk type as whole milk per accepted suggestion.
Detailed incubator equipment as an electric yogurt maker or Instant Pot set to 110°F per accepted suggestion.
